Main.sentence: Martha's Vineyard , often simply called the Vineyard ,  is an ___E:island U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Island)___ in the U.S. state of ___E:Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts)___ , lying just south of ___E:Cape Cod U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Cod)___ .

It is known for being a popular, affluent ___E:summer colony U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_colony)___ , and includes the smaller peninsula ___E:Chappaquiddick Island U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chappaquiddick_Island)___ .

It is the ___E:58th largest island U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_islands_of_the_United_States_by_area)___ in the U.S., with a land area of about 96 square miles (250 km 2 ),  and the third-largest on the ___E:East Coast U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Coast_of_the_United_States)___ , after ___E:Long Island U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_Island)___ and ___E:Mount Desert Island U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Desert_Island)___ .

Martha's Vineyard constitutes the bulk of ___E:Dukes County, Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dukes_County,_Massachusetts)___ , which also includes the ___E:Elizabeth Islands U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_Islands)___ and the island of ___E:Nomans Land U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nomans_Land_(Massachusetts))___ .
The island's year-round population has considerably increased since the 1960s.
In the 2023 Martha's Vineyard Commission report, the year-round population was 20,530, an increase from 16,460 in 2010.  The summer population swells to more than 200,000 people.
About 56 percent of the Vineyard's 14,621 homes are seasonally occupied.
A study by the Martha's Vineyard Commission in 2006 found that the cost of living on the island is 60 percent higher than the national average, and housing prices are 96 percent higher.

A study of housing needs by the Commission found that the average weekly wage on Martha's Vineyard was "71 percent of the state average, the median home price was 54 percent above the state's and the median rent exceeded the state's by 17 percent," all leading to a stark example of severe income inequalities between year-round residents and their seasonal counterparts.

Though many have suggested that the island was renamed after English explorer ___E:Bartholomew Gosnold U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bartholomew_Gosnold)___ 's daughter Martha, it is more likely that both the island and his daughter were namesakes of his wealthy mother-in-law, Martha (Judde) Golding, who partly funded his expedition in 1602 – the first recorded European expedition to ___E:Cape Cod U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Cod)___ . [a] A smaller island to the south was first to be named "Martha's Vineyard" but this later became associated with this island.
It is the eighth-oldest surviving English place-name in the United States.
The island was subsequently known as Martin's Vineyard (possibly after a captain in the exploratory party, John Martin); many people and maps up to the 18th century called it by this name.

When the ___E:United States Board on Geographic Names U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Board_on_Geographic_Names)___ worked to standardize placename spellings in the late 19th century, apostrophes were dropped.

Thus for a time Martha's Vineyard was officially named Marthas Vineyard , but the Board reversed its decision in the early 20th century, making Martha's Vineyard one of the five placenames in the United States that takes a ___E:possessive apostrophe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apostrophe#Possessives_in_geographic_names)___ . [b]
According to historian Henry Franklin Norton, the island was known by Native Americans as Noepe or Capawock .

It is referred to in the 1691 ___E:Massachusetts Charter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts_Charter)___ (which transferred the island from the ___E:Province of New York U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Province_of_New_York)___ during the breakup of the ___E:Dominion of New England U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominion_of_New_England)___ ) as Cappawock .

The island was originally inhabited by ___E:Wampanoag people U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wampanoag_people)___ , when Martha's Vineyard was known in the ___E:Massachusett language U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusett_language)___ as Noepe , or "land amid the streams".
In 1642, the Wampanoag numbered somewhere around 3,000 on the island.
By 1764, that number had dropped to 313.

___E:European settlement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_colonization_of_the_Americas)___ began with the purchase of Martha's Vineyard, ___E:Nantucket U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nantucket)___ , and the Elizabeth Islands by ___E:Thomas Mayhew U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Mayhew_(governor))___ of ___E:Watertown, Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watertown,_Massachusetts)___ , from two New England settlers.
He had friendly relations with the Wampanoags on the island, in part because he was careful to honor their land rights.

His son, also named Thomas Mayhew, established the first settlement on the island in 1642 at Great Harbor (later ___E:Edgartown, Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgartown,_Massachusetts)___ ).

The younger Mayhew began a relationship with ___E:Hiacoomes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hiacoomes)___ , a ___E:Native American U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Americans_in_the_United_States)___ neighbor, which eventually led to Hiacoomes' family converting to ___E:Christianity U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christianity)___ .

During ___E:King Philip's War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Philip%27s_War)___ later in the century, the Martha's Vineyard band did not join their tribal relatives in the uprising and remained armed, a testimony to the good relations cultivated by the Mayhews as the leaders of the colony. [citation needed] In 1657, the younger Thomas Mayhew was drowned when a ship he was travelling in was lost at sea on a voyage to England.

Mayhew's grandsons ___E:Matthew Mayhew U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthew_Mayhew)___ (1648–), John Mayhew (1652–), and other members of his family assisted him in running his business and government.
In 1665, Mayhew's lands were included in a grant to the ___E:Duke of York U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_II_of_England)___ .

In 1671, a settlement was arranged which allowed Mayhew to continue in his position while placing his territory under the jurisdiction of the ___E:Province of New York U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Province_of_New_York)___ .
In 1682, Matthew Mayhew succeeded his grandfather as Governor and Chief Magistrate, and occasionally preached to the Native Americans.

He was also appointed judge of the Court of Common Pleas for Dukes county in 1697, and remained on the bench until 1700. He was judge of probate from 1696 to 1710.  In 1683, ___E:Dukes County, New York U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dukes_County,_New_York)___ was incorporated, including Martha's Vineyard.

In 1691, at the collapse of rule by Sir ___E:Edmund Andros U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edmund_Andros)___ and the reorganization of Massachusetts as a royal colony, Dukes County was transferred to the ___E:Province of Massachusetts Bay U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Province_of_Massachusetts_Bay)___ , and split into the county of ___E:Dukes County, Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dukes_County,_Massachusetts)___ and ___E:Nantucket County, Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nantucket_County,_Massachusetts)___ . [citation needed] Following the revocation of the Massachusetts Bay Colony Charter in 1684, ___E:William Coddington Jr. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Coddington_Jr.)___ , who was governor of ___E:Rhode Island U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhode_Island)___ at the time, attempted to seize Martha's Vineyard through a group of militia as "reparations for former damages of past leaders made by the settlers,"  most likely referring to the ___E:Puritan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puritan)___ actions on ___E:Rhode Island U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhode_Island)___ leaders ___E:Roger Williams U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Williams)___ and ___E:Anne Hutchinson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anne_Hutchinson)___ , as well as annex threats made by Massachusetts.

It is possible that ___E:Coddington U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Coddington_Jr.)___ only wanted to annex Martha's Vineyard due to its proximity to Rhode Island and the fact that it would have taken more labor for colonists in Massachusetts to reach Martha's Vineyard before Rhode Island could obtain full control of the island.

The plan flopped: on the week that was taken to go to the island, Rhode Island militiamen were deployed in a group of three boats and "upon seeing men on Martha's Vineyard, the men immediately fled the vicinity of the island and returned home after The Governor dispatched them from their duties and made the plan defunct".

There is still wide debate as to who told leaders from Massachusetts about the plan. One story has prevailed, that a traveler going to and from Rhode Island and Massachusetts for business purposes heard the claim and reported it back to officials in Massachusetts.
Massachusetts, specifically Martha's Vineyard, was not intimidated by this attempt and thought Rhode Island to be weaker because of their immediate retreat.

As for the history following the attempted annexation, Native American literacy in the schools founded by Thomas Mayhew Jr. and taught by ___E:Peter Folger U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Foulger)___ (the grandfather of ___E:Benjamin Franklin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_Franklin)___ ) was such that the first Native American graduates of Harvard were from Martha's Vineyard, including the son of Hiacoomes, ___E:Joel Hiacoomes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joel_Hiacoomes)___ . "The ship Joel Hiacoomes was sailing on, as he was returning to Boston from a trip home shortly before the graduation ceremonies, was found wrecked on the shores of Nantucket Island. ___E:Caleb Cheeshahteaumauk U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caleb_Cheeshahteaumuck)___ , the son of a sachem of Homes Hole, did graduate from Harvard in the class of 1665."  Cheeshahteaumauk's Latin address to the corporation (New England Corporation), which begins "Honoratissimi benefactores" (most honored benefactors), has been preserved.
In addition to speaking Wampanoag and ___E:English U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_language)___ , they studied Hebrew, classical Greek, and Latin.
All of the early Native American graduates died shortly after completing their course of study.
Many native preachers on the island, however, also preached in the ___E:Christian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christianity)___ churches from time to time. [citation needed]

Mayhew's successor as leader of the community was the Hon. Leavitt Thaxter,  who married Martha Mayhew, a descendant of Thomas Mayhew, and was an Edgartown educator described by Indian Commissioner ___E:John Milton Earle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Milton_Earle)___ as "a long and steadfast friend to the Indians."  After living in ___E:Northampton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northampton,_Massachusetts)___ , Thaxter, a lawyer,  returned home to Edgartown, where he took over the school founded by his father, Rev. Joseph Thaxter,   and served in the State ___E:House U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts_House_of_Representatives)___ and the ___E:Senate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts_Senate)___ , was a member of the ___E:Massachusetts Governor's Council U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts_Governor%27s_Council)___ , and later served as ___E:U. S. Customs Collector U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Customs_Service)___ for Martha's Vineyard.

Having rechristened his father's Edgartown school Thaxter Academy, on February 15, 1845, Thaxter was granted the sum of $50 per year for "the support of William Johnson, an Indian of the Chappequiddic tribe." By this time, Leavitt Thaxter  had taken on the role, described in an act passed by the ___E:General Court of Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Court_of_Massachusetts)___ , as "guardian of the Indians and people of color resident at Chappequiddic and Indiantown in the County of Dukes County."  Thaxter Academy, founded by Leavitt Thaxter as first principal in 1825, became known for educating both white and Native American youth.

Like the nearby island of ___E:Nantucket U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nantucket)___ , Martha's Vineyard was brought to prominence in the 19th century by the ___E:whaling U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whaling)___ industry, during which ships were sent around the world to hunt whales for their oil and ___E:blubber U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blubber)___ .

The discovery of ___E:petroleum U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petroleum)___ in ___E:Pennsylvania U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvania)___ gave rise to a cheaper source of oil for lamps and led to an almost complete collapse of the industry by 1870. After the Old Colony railroad came to mainland Woods Hole in 1872, summer residences began to develop on the island, such as the community of ___E:Harthaven U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harthaven)___ established by William H. Hart, and later, the community of Ocean Heights, developed near Sengekontacket Pond in ___E:Edgartown U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgartown)___ by the prominent island businessman, Robert Marsden Laidlaw.

Although the island struggled financially through the ___E:Great Depression U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Depression)___ , its reputation as a ___E:resort U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resort)___ for ___E:tourists U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tourist)___ and the wealthy continued to grow. There is still a substantial Wampanoag population on the Vineyard, mainly located in the town of ___E:Aquinnah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aquinnah,_Massachusetts)___ .
Aquinnah means "land under the hill" in the Wampanoag language. [citation needed]

The island was the last refuge of the ___E:heath hen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heath_hen)___ , an extinct subspecies of the ___E:greater prairie chicken U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_prairie_chicken)___ , which was a once common game bird throughout the ___E:Northeastern United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northeastern_United_States)___ .
Despite 19th century efforts to protect the hen, by 1927, the population of birds had dropped to 13. The last known heath hen, named "Booming Ben", perished on Martha's Vineyard in 1932.
Martha's Vineyard was used by the Army, Navy and Air Force from 1941 through 1945 for training missions that ranged from landings on beaches to climbing cliffs and bombing practice.

The linguist ___E:William Labov U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Labov)___ wrote his ___E:master's thesis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Arts)___ on changes in the Martha's Vineyard dialect of English.
The 1963 study is widely recognized as a seminal work in the foundation of ___E:sociolinguistics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sociolinguistics)___ .

The island received international notoriety after the " ___E:Chappaquiddick incident U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chappaquiddick_incident)___ " of July 18, 1969, in which ___E:Mary Jo Kopechne U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_Jo_Kopechne)___ was killed in a car driven off the Dike Bridge by U.S.
Senator ___E:Edward "Ted" Kennedy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Kennedy)___ .
The bridge crossed Poucha Pond on ___E:Chappaquiddick Island U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chappaquiddick_Island)___ (a smaller island formerly connected to the Vineyard and part of Edgartown).
The bridge was intended for people on foot and ___E:bicycles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicycle)___ , as well as the occasional emergency vehicle when conditions warranted.
Currently, ___E:4×4 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/4%C3%974)___ vehicles with passes are allowed to cross the reconstructed bridge.

On November 23, 1970, in the Atlantic Ocean just west of Aquinnah, ___E:Simas Kudirka U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simas_Kudirka)___ , a Soviet seaman of ___E:Lithuanian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lithuania)___ nationality, ___E:attempted to defect U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_United_States_Coast_Guard#The_Kudirka_incident)___ to the United States by leaping onto a ___E:United States Coast Guard U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Coast_Guard)___ cutter from a Soviet fishing trawler and asking for asylum.

The Coast Guard allowed a detachment of four seamen from the Soviet ship to board the cutter and "drag the kicking, screaming Kudirka back to their vessel." He was sentenced to 10 years of hard labor in the Soviet Union.

In 1974, ___E:Steven Spielberg U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Spielberg)___ filmed the movie Jaws on Martha's Vineyard, most notably in the fishing village of ___E:Menemsha U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Menemsha)___ and the town of ___E:Chilmark U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilmark,_Massachusetts)___ .

Spielberg selected island natives Christopher Rebello as Chief Brody's oldest son, Michael Brody; Jay Mello as the younger son, Sean Brody; and ___E:Lee Fierro U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Fierro)___ as Mrs. Kintner.
Scores of other island natives appeared in the film as ___E:extras U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extra_(actor))___ .
Later, scenes from Jaws 2 and Jaws: The Revenge were filmed on the island, as well. In June 2005 the island celebrated the 30th anniversary of Jaws with a weekend-long Jawsfest.

In 1977, distressed over losing their guaranteed seat in the Massachusetts General Court, inhabitants of Martha's Vineyard considered the possibility of ___E:secession U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secession)___ from the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, either to become part of another state (having received offers from both ___E:Vermont U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vermont)___ and ___E:Hawaii U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii)___ ), reincorporating as a separate U.S. territory, or as the nation's ___E:51st state U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/51st_state)___ .
The separatist flag, consisting of a white seagull over an orange disk on a sky-blue background, is still seen on the island today.
Although the idea of separation from Massachusetts eventually proved impracticable, it did receive attention in the local, regional, and even national media.

On March 5, 1982, ___E:John Belushi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Belushi)___ died of a drug overdose in Los Angeles, California, and was buried four days later in Abel's Hill Cemetery in Chilmark.
Belushi often visited the Vineyard and his family felt it fitting to bury him there.

On his gravestone is the quote: "Though I may be gone, Rock 'N' Roll lives on." Because of the many visitors to his grave and the threat of vandalism, his body was moved somewhere near the grave site. His grave remains a popular site for visitors to Chilmark and they often leave tokens in memory of the late comedian.

Since the 1990s, ___E:Bill Clinton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton)___ has spent regular vacation time on the island during and after his presidency, along with his wife, ___E:Hillary Clinton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillary_Clinton)___ , and their daughter, ___E:Chelsea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton)___ .

Clinton was not the first president to visit the islands; ___E:Ulysses S. Grant U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ulysses_S._Grant)___ visited the vacation residence of his friend, Bishop ___E:Gilbert Haven U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gilbert_Haven)___ on August 24, 1874. As a coincidental footnote in history, Bishop Haven's ___E:gingerbread cottage U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gingerbread_(architecture))___ was located in Oak Bluffs at 10 Clinton Avenue.
The avenue was named in 1851 and was designated as the main promenade of the ___E:Martha's Vineyard Campmeeting Association campgrounds U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wesleyan_Grove)___ .
In December 2019, President ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ completed the purchase of a 30-acre (12 ha) homestead on the Edgartown Great Pond.

On July 16, 1999, a ___E:small plane crashed U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_Jr._plane_crash)___ off the coast of Martha's Vineyard, claiming the lives of pilot ___E:John F. Kennedy Jr. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_Jr.)___ , his wife ___E:Carolyn Bessette U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolyn_Bessette)___ , and her sister Lauren Bessette.

Kennedy's mother, former U.S. first lady ___E:Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacqueline_Kennedy_Onassis)___ , maintained a home in Aquinnah (formerly "Gay Head") until her death in 1994.

In the summer of 2000, an outbreak of ___E:tularemia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tularemia)___ , also known as rabbit fever, resulted in one death and piqued the interest of the ___E:CDC U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centers_for_Disease_Control_and_Prevention)___ , which wanted to test the island as a potential investigative ground for aerosolized Francisella tularensis .

Over the following summers, Martha's Vineyard was identified as the only place in the world where documented cases of tularemia resulted from ___E:lawn mowing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawn_mowing)___ .

The research could prove valuable in preventing ___E:bioterrorism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bioterrorism)___ . [citation needed] In the television show The X-Files , ___E:Fox Mulder U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_Mulder)___ 's parents live on the island,  and it was also the setting for Robert Harris' 2007 novel The Ghost .

In September 2022, Florida governor ___E:Ron DeSantis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_DeSantis)___ flew two planeloads of Venezuelan ___E:migrants to Martha's Vineyard U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha%27s_Vineyard_migrant_crisis)___ in an effort to draw attention to what Republican governors consider "the Biden administration's failed border policies".
Some observers criticized DeSantis because the migrants were flown there unannounced.
For nearly two days, island residents provided clothing, food, toys, toiletries, and temporary shelter, before removing the migrants from the island.
People were bought, sold, and probated as property on Martha's Vineyard.

In 1700, Reverend ___E:Samuel Sewall U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_Sewall)___ , a seasonal resident of Martha's Vineyard, was one of the first to publicly oppose slavery in the New England Colonies.
In 1646, magistrates in Massachusetts ruled that two Africans who had been enslaved and imported be returned to their native country.
In 1652, Rhode Island passed a law abolishing slavery and ordering that Africans be freed after a term of 10 years, just like indentured servants.
In addition to that, "at no time during its history did people of color lose the right to use the courts to challenge their status.
Nor did they lose the right to inherit property in certain circumstances."

On October 15, 2020, Edgartown Harbor was officially recognized as an ___E:Underground Railroad U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Underground_Railroad)___ Site by the ___E:National Park Service U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Park_Service)___ .
This recognition was given after a submission from a nonprofit corporation, the African American Heritage Trail of Martha's Vineyard.
The corporation was founded in 1998 by Martha's Vineyard NAACP vice president Carrie Camillo Tankard and teacher Elaine Cawley Weintraub.

Their mission is to "continue to research and publish previously undocumented history and to involve the Island community in the identification and celebration of the contributions made by people of color to the island of Martha's Vineyard."  The trail consists of 31 sites all marked by a descriptive plaque.
Martha's Vineyard became known as an "everyone signs" community after three centuries of an unusually high level of hereditary deafness  caused Martha's Vineyard to be labeled a "deaf utopia".

The island's deaf heritage cannot be traced to one common ancestor and is thought to have originated in the ___E:Weald U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weald)___ , a region that overlaps the borders of the English counties of ___E:Kent U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kent)___ and ___E:Sussex U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sussex)___ , prior to immigration.

Researcher Nora Groce estimates that by the late 19th century, one in 155 people on the Vineyard was born deaf (0.7 percent) — about 37 times the estimate for the nation at large (1 in 5,728, or 0.02 percent)  — because of a "recessive pattern" of genetic deafness, circulated through ___E:endogamous U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endogamous)___ marriage patterns.
Deaf Vineyarders generally earned an average or above-average income (proved by tax records) and they participated in church affairs with passion.
The deafness on the island affected both females and males in approximately the same percentage.

In the late 19th century, the mixed marriages between deaf and hearing spouses comprised 65 percent of all deaf marriages on the island, as compared to the rate of 20 percent deaf-hearing marriage in the mainland.

The sign language used by Vineyarders is called ___E:Martha's Vineyard Sign Language (MVSL) U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha%27s_Vineyard_Sign_Language)___ , and it is different from ___E:American Sign Language U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Sign_Language)___ (ASL).
However, the geographical, time, and population proximities state that MVSL and ASL are impossible to develop in complete isolation from each other.
MVSL was commonly used by hearing residents as well as deaf ones until the middle of the 20th century.
No language barrier created a smooth communication environment for all the residents of the island.
In the 20th century, tourism became a mainstay in the island economy, and new tourism-related jobs appeared.

However, jobs in tourism were not as deaf-friendly as fishing and farming had been. Consequently, as intermarriage and further migration joined the people of Martha's Vineyard to the mainland, the island community more and more resembled the oral community there.

The last deaf person born into the island's sign-language tradition, Katie West, died in 1952, but a few elderly residents were able to recall MVSL as recently as the 1980s when research into the language began.

According to the ___E:Köppen climate classification U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification)___ system, the climate of the island borders between a ___E:humid continental climate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humid_continental_climate)___ ( Dfa / Dfb ), a ___E:humid subtropical climate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humid_subtropical_climate)___ ( Cfa ), and an ___E:oceanic climate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oceanic_climate)___ ( Cfb ), the latter a climate type rarely found on the east coast of North America.

Martha's Vineyard's climate is highly influenced by the surrounding ___E:Atlantic Ocean U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Ocean)___ , which moderates temperatures throughout the year, although this moderation is nowhere near as strong as on opposite sides of the Atlantic ( ___E:Porto U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porto#Climate)___ , ___E:Portugal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portugal)___ ) or the Pacific coast of the United States ( ___E:Crescent City U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crescent_City,_California#Climate)___ ) at similar latitudes.
As a result, winter temperatures tend to be a few degrees warmer while summer temperatures tend to be cooler than inland locations.
Winters are cool to cold with a January average of just slightly below 32 °F (0.0 °C).
Owing to the influence of the Atlantic Ocean, temperatures below 0 °F (−17.8 °C) are rare, occurring at one day per year, with most days during the winter months rising above freezing.
The average annual snowfall is 25.3 inches (643 mm).

Summers are warm and mild with temperatures rarely exceeding 90 °F (32.2 °C), with only one or two days reaching or exceeding it.  During the summer months, the island's warmest months (July and August) average around 71.5 °F (21.9 °C)

Spring and fall are transition seasons with spring being cooler than fall. The highest daily maximum temperature was 99 °F (37.2 °C) on August 27, 1948, and the highest daily minimum temperature was 76 °F (24.4 °C) on September 4, 2010. The lowest daily maximum temperature was 7 °F (−13.9 °C) on December 26, 1980, and the lowest daily minimum temperature was −9 °F (−22.8 °C) on February 2 and 3, 1961.  Martha's Vineyard receives 46.94 inches (1,192 mm) of ___E:precipitation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Precipitation_(meteorology))___ per year, which is evenly distributed throughout the year. The ___E:hardiness zone U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hardiness_zone)___ is 7a in the central and most of the western areas of the main island and 7b on the east end including Chappaquiddick and the southwest end.
Martha's Vineyard is divided into six towns.

Each town is governed by a ___E:Board of Selectmen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_of_Selectmen)___ elected by town voters in each of the towns, along with annual and periodic ___E:town meetings U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Town_meeting)___ .
Each town is also a member of the Martha's Vineyard Commission, which regulates island-wide building, environmental, and aesthetic concerns.
Some government programs on the island—such as the public school system, emergency management, and waste management—have been regionalized.
There is a growing push for further regionalization areas of law enforcement, water treatment, and possible government regionalization. [citation needed]
Each town also follows certain regulations from Dukes County.
The towns are: [citation needed]

The three "Down-Island" towns of ___E:Edgartown U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgartown,_Massachusetts)___ , ___E:Tisbury U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tisbury,_Massachusetts)___ , and ___E:Oak Bluffs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oak_Bluffs,_Massachusetts)___ are "wet" towns—serving alcohol. ___E:West Tisbury U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Tisbury,_Massachusetts)___ and ___E:Aquinnah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aquinnah,_Massachusetts)___ are "soggy" towns that serve only beer and wine, and ___E:Chilmark U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilmark,_Massachusetts)___ is a "dry" town.
Martha's Vineyard is accessible via ferry.

The ___E:Steamship Authority U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steamship_Authority)___ operates year-round ferry service from ___E:Woods Hole, Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woods_Hole,_Massachusetts)___ .
This is the only ferry that can transport vehicles to and from the island.
Seasonal ferry services depart from Falmouth, Hyannis, and New Bedford in Massachusetts, North Kingstown in Rhode Island, and limited service from New York City to New Jersey.

___E:Martha's Vineyard Airport U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha%27s_Vineyard_Airport)___ (MVY) is the main airport on the island. ___E:Cape Air U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Air)___ provides year-round service to and from ___E:Boston U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logan_International_Airport)___ and ___E:New York City U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_International_Airport)___ .

Seasonal destinations include ___E:Hyannis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barnstable_Municipal_Airport)___ , ___E:New Bedford U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Bedford_Regional_Airport)___ , ___E:Nantucket U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nantucket_Memorial_Airport)___ , White Plains, New York, ___E:Washington-Reagan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington-Reagan)___ , ___E:New York-LaGuardia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LaGuardia_Airport)___ , ___E:Philadelphia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_Airport)___ and ___E:Charlotte U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlotte_Douglas_International_Airport)___ . ___E:JetBlue U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JetBlue)___ , ___E:Delta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delta_Air_Lines)___ , ___E:American Airlines U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Airlines)___ , and ___E:Elite Airways U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elite_Airways)___ operate seasonal flights from New York City and Boston.
The ___E:Martha's Vineyard Transit Authority U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha%27s_Vineyard_Transit_Authority)___ (VTA) provides year-round bus service throughout Martha's Vineyard.

In the era before modern highways and jet planes, travelers took ___E:New York, New Haven & Hartford Railroad U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York,_New_Haven_%26_Hartford_Railroad)___ trains from ___E:New York City U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City)___ or ___E:Boston U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston)___ to Woods Hole or Hyannis, at which point they would embark on ferries to the island.
Martha's Vineyard is served by Martha's Vineyard Public Schools:

The six towns of Edgartown, Oak Bluffs, Tisbury, West Tisbury, Chilmark, and Aquinnah are each served by local K–8 or K–5 schools (Aquinnah and Chilmark are split between Chilmark for elementary and West Tisbury for middle school), and all feed into the regional high school.
Additionally, the K–12 public charter school in West Tisbury is open to students from any town on the island.
During the whaling era, wealthy ___E:Boston U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston)___ sea captains and merchant traders often created estates on Martha's Vineyard with their trading profits.

Today, the Vineyard has become one of the ___E:Northeastern United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northeastern_United_States)___ ' most prominent summering havens, having attracted numerous celebrity regulars.

The island now has a year-round population of about 20,530 people in six towns; in summer, the population increases to 200,000 residents,  with more than 25,000 additional short-term visitors coming and going on the ___E:ferries U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferry)___ during the summer season.

The most crowded weekend is July 4, followed by the late-August weekend of the Agricultural Fair. In general, the summer season runs from June through Labor Day weekend, coinciding with the months most American children are not in school.

In 1985, the two islands of Martha's Vineyard and Chappaquiddick Island were included in a new ___E:American Viticultural Area U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Viticultural_Area)___ designation for ___E:wine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wine)___ ___E:appellation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appellation)___ of origin specification: ___E:Martha's Vineyard AVA U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha%27s_Vineyard_AVA)___ .
Wines produced from ___E:grapes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grape)___ grown on the two islands can be sold with labels that carry the Martha's Vineyard AVA designation.
Martha's Vineyard was the home to the winemaker Chicama Vineyards in West Tisbury, though it closed after 37 years on August 10, 2008.

Other popular attractions include the annual ___E:Grand Illumination U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Illumination)___ in Oak Bluffs; the Martha's Vineyard Film Center, an arthouse cinema which is run by the non-profit Martha's Vineyard Film Society,  and which screens independent and world cinema all year long; the historic Capawock and Strand theatres, also run by the Martha's Vineyard Film Society, the Martha's Vineyard Film Festival,  which runs a winter film festival in March, a Summer Film Series and Cinema Circus every Wednesday in July and August, the ___E:Martha's Vineyard African-American Film Festival U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha%27s_Vineyard_African_American_Film_Festival)___ ,  which showcases the works of independent and established African-American filmmakers in August, and Martha's Vineyard International Film Festival in September; the Farm Institute at Katama Farm in Edgartown;  and the ___E:Flying Horses Carousel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flying_Horses_Carousel)___ in Oak Bluffs, the oldest operating platform ___E:carousel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carousel)___ in the United States. [citation needed]

Across the Edgartown Vineyard Haven Road from the ___E:Martha's Vineyard Regional High School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha%27s_Vineyard_Regional_High_School)___ in the town of Oak Bluffs, the ___E:Martha's Vineyard Skatepark U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha%27s_Vineyard_Skatepark)___ is a concrete skatepark open to the public, offering a range of ramps and obstacles.
Its relatively small year-round population has led to a very activist citizenry who are highly involved in the island's day-to-day activities.
Tourism, overdevelopment, politics, and environmentalism are of keen interest to the community.

Keeping the balance between the much needed tourist economy and the ___E:ecology U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecology)___ and ___E:wildlife U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wildlife)___ of the island is of paramount importance to residents.
In contrast to the seasonal influx of wealthy visitors, Dukes County remains one of the poorest in the state.

Residents have established resources to balance the contradictions and stresses that can arise in these circumstances, notably the Martha's Vineyard Commission  and Martha's Vineyard Community Services,  founded by the late Dr. Milton Mazer, author of People and Predicaments: Of Life and Distress on Martha's Vineyard .
The majority of the Vineyard's residents during the summer are well-established seasonal vacationers.

While many of these come from all over the United States and abroad, the island tends to be a destination for especially those whose primary residence lies within close proximity in the Northeastern U.S.
Many communities around the island tend to have deep family roots on the island that have matured over the years to create hamlets of good friends and neighbors.
Nevertheless, many visitors are summer renters and weekenders, for whom the island is simply a "home away from home". [citation needed]

Despite popular perceptions of the Vineyard as "Hollywood East", the island is very low-key and quiet; celebrities go to the Vineyard to enjoy the atmosphere, and not to be seen. Locals tend to be protective of ___E:celebrity privacy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_privacy)___ , though recent coverage of celebrity sightings (most notably in the two local newspapers on the Island) has begun to erode that respect for privacy through more frequent reporting on celebrity sightings and famous visitors.

In August 2014, both President Obama and Hillary Clinton planned to have overlapping visits to the island, where the presence of security details that create traffic challenges is becoming an annual affair.
Many of the country's most affluent African-American families have enjoyed a century-old tradition of summering on the island.

Concentrated primarily in and around the town of Oak Bluffs, and the East Chop area, these families have historically represented the black elite from Boston, Washington, D.C., and New York City. Today, affluent families from around the country have taken to the Vineyard, and the community is known as a popular summer destination for judges, physicians, business executives, surgeons, attorneys, writers, politicians, and professors.

The historic presence of African-American residents in Oak Bluffs resulted in its Town Beach being pejoratively called "The Inkwell", a nickname which was ___E:reappropriated U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reappropriation)___ as an emblem of pride.

The Inkwell (1994), directed by ___E:Matty Rich U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matty_Rich)___ , dealt with this close-knit Vineyard community. [citation needed] The Run&Shoot Filmworks Martha's Vineyard African-American Film Festival, held every second week in August, highlights the works of independent and established filmmakers from across the globe.
This annual event draws attendees from all across the world.

Since the 19th century, the island has had a sizable community of ___E:Portuguese-Americans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese-Americans)___ , concentrated primarily in the three down-Island towns of Oak Bluffs, Tisbury, and Edgartown; they have traditionally worked alongside other island residents in whaling and fishing.

It also has a large community of ___E:Brazilian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_diaspora)___ ___E:immigrants U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immigration_to_the_United_States)___ who work mainly in the maintenance of the island's vacation facilities.
The island's permanent residents were profiled in a London Telegraph article showing "the dark side of Martha's Vineyard".

In the same month an article titled "Edgartown's Darker Side" appeared in the Boston Globe detailing the extremely poor working conditions suffered by Irish and Serbian students in a newly built private members club in Edgartown.

Concerns over munitions that may be buried on Martha's Vineyard, most from World War II,  have led to an 8.1 million dollar project to remove and rebuild part of a privately owned barrier beach off the ___E:Tisbury Great Pond U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tisbury_Great_Pond)___ .

The year-round working population of Martha's Vineyard earns 30 percent less on average than other residents of the state while keeping up with a cost of living that is 60 percent higher than average.

Many people are moving to more affordable areas. [citation needed] Schools have seen a successive drop in enrollment over the past few years. [citation needed] Typically home to artists, musicians, and other creative types, the Island has many residents who manage by working several jobs in the summer and taking some time off in the winter. [citation needed] The lack of affordable housing on the island has forced many families to move off-island. [citation needed]

Many high-profile residents, movie stars, politicians, writers, and artists contribute to fundraisers and benefits that raise awareness of the fragile ecosystem of the Vineyard and support community organizations and services.
The largest of these is the annual Possible Dreams Auction.
Television broadcasts are available using varied methods from nearby broadcast markets.
